chapter: Chicago pioneers, community and New Orleans brotherhood
title: Mama Yancey, Billie Holiday and playing with heroes
summary: Anecdotes of Mama Yancey singing, Billie Holiday sitting in at the DeLisa, and DeMichael's thrills playing with Bobby Hackett, Vic Dickenson and Buck Clayton.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Right, right. I -- she drinks an awful lot, but I had the pleasure of seeing Mama Yancey not too long ago.
Yeah, yeah.
And she was at a party and she sang. But she's almost blind now.
I know, one of the great thrills of the last year or so in my life, was -- I was playing Jazz at Noon.
Yeah, right, right.
And she came in with Erwin Helfer.
Oh, yeah, right, the piano player, right.
Very much like Yancey.
Right, right.
And they came up and did a couple of things. And I got to play behind her.
Right, right.
(Inaudible.)
Right, she sings --
That was a great honor for me.

Right, right. She sang the blues. These are the things that are so rewarding to a musician, like, down through the years, when I was at the club, at the DeLisa and things like that, and we dragged the people up, and I'd get Billie Holiday and she'd come up and sing some tunes with us and things like that.
These are the things that -- they're treasures.
That's right. I've had experiences like that in the last few years, getting to play gigs with --
Right.
-- men that I've admired ever since I got into some of the music, Bobby Hackett, Vic Dickenson.
Right, Bobby, Vic, right, right, right.
Wild Bill.
Right, right, right.
